title: Push depth further: 10 -> 12 layers at constant width 512
description: DEPTH 10 -> 12 and ASPECT_RATIO 48 -> 40 so model_dim stays 512 with 4 heads of 128; pure depth change, nothing else touched.
reflection: POSITIVE: val_bpb 0.986443 vs baseline 0.989007, better by 0.0026 (~3x the ~0.0009 noise floor). Numbers: 71.3M params (was 60.8M), FLOPs/token 3.46e8 (was 2.96e8, +17%), total_tokens 331.2M (was 381.2M, -13%), 2527 steps, steady-state MFU 38.45% (was 37.82%), peak VRAM 32.9GB (was 27.1GB), still epoch 1. The depth axis is still climbing but the marginal return is shrinking fast: 8->10 bought -0.0084, 10->12 bought only -0.0026 for a similar relative FLOP cost. Extrapolating, 12->14 is worth maybe -0.001, i.e. at or below the noise floor, and it would push VRAM toward ~38GB and cut tokens another 12%. I would NOT spend a slot on depth 14; the depth ramp is close to exhausted at this 300s budget. The untouched axis with the best prior now is WIDTH (ASPECT_RATIO up so model_dim goes 512 -> 640, keeping 5 heads of 128), or the schedule/regularization knobs nobody has probed (WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5, WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2, softcap, WINDOW_PATTERN). Note MFU barely moved this time (37.8 -> 38.5), so the free amortization bonus that made 8->10 cheap is also spent.
